chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who looks at a believer with a look intended to frighten him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will frighten him on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: the Day when there is no shade except His Shade

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of frightening a believer with a look?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the spiritual gravity of non-verbal aggression, linking the mundane act of a fearful gaze to the ultimate divine recompense on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the sanctity of the believer's peace of mind, warning that causing anxiety to a fellow believer incurs a direct fear from Allah when all other sources of comfort vanish.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Ansary, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who looks towards a Momin with a (frightening) look in order to scare him with, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Scare him on the Day on which there be no shade except for Hisazwj Shade’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Ansari from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever looks upon a believer to frighten him, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will frighten him on the day when there will be no shadow (protection), accept His shadow.’”
